scope: Authorized full-pool short learning; at most 1024 updates; no external weights or automatic budget extension.
question: Does broader existing training exposure improve fixed development ranking and difficult-normal protection beyond micro learning?
sampling: original 240-world probabilities in results/coverage/sampling.npz; SeedSequence([seed,7,draw]); two complete scans per update

evaluation.train_scope: fixed training-source diagnostic set; exact world-frame request counts reported; membership does not imply exposure
evaluation.synthetic_targets: all valid frozen labels including zero-anomaly and fewer-than-five-return frames; official filter secondary
evaluation.thresholds: each checkpoint's complete 206 diagnostic pool chooses the 1% FPR threshold; apply it unchanged to 201, zero-anomaly frames and both scans of each normal pair; real subgroup counts use that checkpoint's pooled real threshold
evaluation.paired_reference: results/micro/256.pt evaluated on the same existing sparse and changed-neighborhood normal witness slots; threshold from results/micro/256.json
evaluation.interpretation: compare short 256 with micro 256 at equal updates; short 1024 changes both sampling exposure and update budget; fixed real 152 is a development subset, not full val19

decision: Evaluate 201 and real AP/FPR95 tradeoffs against micro 256, difficult-normal transitions, 201 middle-return anomalies and real 125. Do not infer useful transfer from training gains alone or automatically extend a stalled development result.
stop: after 1024 updates and declared evaluations, or immediately on numerical failure; preserve state; no automatic parameter retry
